title: MAPR: the documentation standard
subject: docs
summary: Map → Axioms → Purpose → Reference: the shape of every doc, map and ADR, and the rules of the registry.

axioms.text: Each thing is documented in one canonical place, nothing is duplicated.
Documentation is positional: a doc lives at the scaffolding level it governs and applies to everything below it; navigation points to it.
Every doc follows the same structure, so a reader always knows where to look.
The structure runs axiom principles → purpose → reference detail. By reading the axiom principles you should understand the architecture principles and no reference should drift from axioms.
Documentation of reusable domains (example: shared libs and seed slices) separates **consumer** (how to use) from **contributor** (how to change).

purpose.intro: Agents write verbose, drifting prose by default, and no human can re-read every doc on every change. MAPR fixes the shape so the constraints are impossible to miss because every doc leads with its what and why before the how.

reference.statement: MAPR stands for Map → Axioms → Purpose → Reference. Three artifacts, one job each.

claims.text: **Map**: navigate. Pointers only, never teaches. It is a `map.json`.
**Doc**: the canonical reference. Axioms → Purpose → Reference. It is a `<id>.json` in a folder of its own.
**ADR**: record one past decision. Context → Decision → Consequences. It is an `adr.json`.
A map that teaches, a doc that records history, or an ADR in a canonical doc are all violations.

reference.statement: Axioms, then purpose, then reference, in that order.

claims.text: **Axioms**: plain sentences. One universal invariant per line, most abstract first, most concrete after. Easy to read, no long prose, no subjectiveness, no method names or shapes.
If it is a mechanism, it is Reference, not an axiom.
**Purpose**: one paragraph, plain dev voice. State why the decisions were made. Do not define universal concepts, do not restate the axioms.
Someone reading the axioms might understand the rules but the purpose of those rules might not be self evident: that is the role of the purpose.
**Reference**: all concrete rules and mechanics that are relevant, still plain dev voice and with diagrams over prose.
**Cross-cutting rationale** is stated once, in the constitution, and referenced. Never repeated per doc.

snippets.caption: <id>/<id>.json
snippets.code:
{
  "id": "<id>",
  "type": "doc",
  "title": "Title",
  "axioms": [ { "text": "numbered sentences, one idea each, abstract to concrete" } ],
  "purpose": { "intro": "one paragraph: why these decisions exist" },
  "reference": [ { "topic": "…", "claims": [ … ] } ]
}

claims.text: The central map is the registry (`docs/engine/registry.ts`): domain entry points only, one per location.
A local map (`<location>/docs/map.json`) points to everything inside that context, nothing outside it.
An entry is a pointer and a one-liner: id, title, path, kind and summary, plus its status.
A map starts with instructions for whoever reads it.
A map of a reusable domain points to `consumer/` and `contributor/` docs, then `adr/` and `glossary/`. Nothing else.

snippets.caption: shared/libs/<name>/docs/
snippets.code:
map.json          ← local map
glossary/         ← the terms
consumer/         ← usage docs (how to use)
contributor/      ← internal docs (how to change)
adr/              ← decisions

examples.title: A location that is not a reusable domain

snippets.caption: apps/main/docs/
snippets.code:
map.json          ← local map
glossary/         ← the terms
<doc>/            ← the docs, flat
adr/              ← decisions

reference.statement: The split applies to reusable domains.

claims.text: Libraries and seed slices are reusable domains: their docs split into `consumer/` and `contributor/`.
The root, main, the apps and infra are not reusable domains: their docs stay flat, with no consumer and no contributor.

reference.statement: An ADR records one past decision.

claims.text: An entry has a date, a title, a context, a decision and consequences, and it is append-only.
A decision that stops being true is superseded by a new entry, never rewritten.
The ADR is stored in `adr/`, beside the docs it concerns.

reference.statement: Every location has its own glossary.

claims.text: Terms are written inline as `[[term]]` or `[[term|shown text]]`.
A term can be used across locations: the viewer reads every glossary at runtime.

reference.statement: A map and an ADR sit with the docs they concern.

claims.text: Global: the registry and the root's `adr/`.
Seed slice: `<slice>/docs/map.json` and `<slice>/docs/adr/`.
Lib: `shared/libs/<name>/docs/map.json` and `…/docs/adr/`.
App: `apps/<name>/docs/map.json` and `…/docs/adr/`.

reference.statement: The order is fixed: axioms approved before reference, never the reverse.

claims.text: Draft the axioms, or the change needed.
Human approves.
Write from scratch, or scan the Reference for gaps and clashes.
Report gaps and clashes to the human.
Human approves the resolution.
Update the Reference.
Human approves the reference.
Update the history in `adr/` if it is an architectural change.

reference.statement: Each file and folder of the registry is labelled mapper compliant or not.

claims.text: A doc is compliant when its id is its folder and file name, it has axioms, a purpose and a reference, and it sits where its location's rules say.
A location is compliant when it has a map, an `adr/` and a `glossary/`, and every file under its docs is in the map or is an asset.
Markdown left in a location is not compliant: it waits in `.old-markdown-to-sunset`.
